item.title: The TUDelft global GRACE(-FO) Level-3 equivalent water height uncertainty product
item.dc:title: The TUDelft global GRACE(-FO) Level-3 equivalent water height uncertainty product
item.dc:creator: Michal Cuadrat-Grzybowski Pieter N. A. M. Visser João de Teixeira da Encarnacao Faculty of Aerospace Engineering, Space Engineering Department, Delft University of Technology, Delft, The NetherlandsMichal Cuadrat-Grzybowski is a PhD researcher in space gravimetry at Delft University of Technology, within the Department of Space Engineering at the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering. His research focuses on high-frequency mass change modelling using GRACE and GRACE-FO satellite gravimetry data. He works on developing and analysing Level-1B and Level-2 based approaches to improve the temporal resolution of terrestrial water storage and mass redistribution signals, with a particular emphasis on uncertainty characterisation and the interpretation of post-fit residuals in gravity field recovery.Pieter N. A. M. Visser is a Full Professor at Delft University of Technology and Head of the Section Astrodynamics & Space Missions at the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering. His research and teaching focus on celestial mechanics and space geodesy, with particular emphasis on precise orbit determination (POD), thermosphere density retrieval from satellite dynamics, and gravity field recovery from space-borne observations. He has made substantial contributions to satellite geodesy and gravity field determination, with a strong focus on exploiting missions such as GRACE and GRACE-FO to improve understanding of mass transport processes within the Earth system.João de Teixeira da Encarnação is an Assistant Professor at Delft University of Technology in the Department of Space Engineering, Faculty of Aerospace Engineering. His research focuses on measuring Earth’s gravity field variations using satellites. With a background in Aerospace Engineering, he works on space accelerometry, estimation theory, and satellite data processing. His main objective is to develop data processing and modelling strategies that maximise the temporal resolution of gravimetric data collected by low-Earth-orbit satellites, as well as to explore the use of small satellite missions for gravimetric and thermospheric applications.
